language: Greek (Arabic-speaking Christian of Damascus; wrote in Greek)
role_place: Damascus-born official at the Umayyad court, later monk at the Mar Saba monastery near Jerusalem, where he wrote the heresiology (De haeresibus) that contains the chapter on the 'Ishmaelites'.
why_relevant: Chapter 101 of De haeresibus (PG 94, 763-773) is the earliest Christian text I read that names Muhammad's wives or a wife-related scandal (Zayd's wife, four wives plus concubines); it does NOT name Aisha and gives no age.
fame: Among the best-known Greek theologians of the 8th century; defender of icons and author of the 'Fount of Knowledge' (Pege gnoseos) and of major hymns still sung in the Eastern churches. Widely read in Byzantine and Western scholastic tradition (Doctor of the Church in the Catholic Church, 1890).
community: Chalcedonian Orthodox (Greek-Melkite tradition of Palestine and Syria)
